TerraTwin: Earth as a Space Laboratory

TerraTwin is an interactive web application designed to help researchers, engineers, and students identify Earth locations suitable for testing technologies intended for future Moon and Mars missions.

Preparing for space exploration requires understanding extreme temperatures, difficult terrain, geological materials, solar energy, and potential water or ice conditions. However, relevant scientific information is often scattered across different databases.

TerraTwin brings these factors together in one accessible platform. Users select a location on an interactive map, explore environmental data from scientific sources such as NASA POWER, and receive an explainable suitability assessment based on six criteria.

The application distinguishes between mapped information, model-based estimates, and missing evidence, making its results more transparent.

By transforming complex Earth observation data into understandable insights, TerraTwin supports educational research, early-stage site screening, and the development of future space exploration technologies.
details:
TerraTwin — Earth as a Space Laboratory

Project Overview

TerraTwin is an interactive web application designed to identify and evaluate locations on Earth that could serve as testing environments for future Moon and Mars exploration technologies.

Space missions require equipment and robotic systems capable of operating in extreme conditions. However, testing technologies directly on the Moon or Mars is expensive and challenging. Certain locations on Earth share geological, climatic, and environmental characteristics with extraterrestrial landscapes, making them useful for early-stage testing.

Our project addresses the challenge of finding and evaluating these terrestrial analog environments using accessible scientific data.

How TerraTwin Works

Users can select any location on an interactive world map or enter geographical coordinates. TerraTwin retrieves available environmental information from scientific sources, including NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, and geological datasets.

The application evaluates six key criteria:

  1. Terrain and slope — elevation and surface complexity.
  2. Geological materials — rock types and estimated surface characteristics.
  3. Temperature extremes — environmental conditions for equipment testing.
  4. Water and ground ice — available evidence and model-based estimates.
  5. Solar energy — potential conditions for solar-powered technologies.
  6. Robotic mobility — terrain suitability for rover testing.

TerraTwin generates an explainable suitability score from 0 to 100, helping users understand whether a location is promising for a selected Earth-based testing scenario.

The platform also provides interactive climate charts, geographical information, research data sources, and scientific explanations.

Importantly, TerraTwin distinguishes between mapped observations, model-based estimates, and unavailable data. Its suitability scores are preliminary screening indicators rather than exact percentages of similarity to another planet.

Technologies Used

TerraTwin was developed primarily using Python and the Streamlit framework.

Additional technologies include:

  • Folium and streamlit-folium for interactive maps.
  • Pandas for environmental data processing.
  • Plotly for scientific charts and visualizations.
  • Requests for communicating with scientific data services.
  • GitHub for source code management.
  • Streamlit Community Cloud for public web hosting.

The application supports English and Ukrainian and includes dark and light interface themes.

Innovation and Creativity

TerraTwin combines environmental data, interactive geographical exploration, and planetary mission requirements within one accessible platform.

Instead of presenting isolated satellite measurements, it transforms multiple environmental characteristics into understandable assessments for potential Earth-based space technology testing.

A key feature is the transparency of its results. Users can examine data sources, understand limitations, and distinguish scientific observations from estimates.

The project brings together Earth science, planetary exploration, programming, and data visualization.

Expected Impact

TerraTwin can help students explore planetary science, support researchers in identifying interesting analog environments, and assist engineers with preliminary evaluation of Earth locations for testing space exploration technologies.

The platform also encourages the educational use of publicly available scientific datasets and makes complex environmental information easier to understand.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, global data coverage, environmental differences between Earth and other planets, accessibility, user experience, and the reliability of estimated information.

Future improvements will focus on deeper integration of lunar and Martian datasets, improved surface analysis, and more detailed comparisons between Earth and planetary environments.

AI Usage Disclosure

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with Python code development, debugging, interface translation, documentation, and presentation preparation.

AI-assisted decorative visuals are labeled in the project presentation. Scientific data are obtained from their original providers, including NASA POWER, and are not presented as AI-generated observations.

Environmental estimates and suitability scores are calculated using the application's algorithms and are distinguished from direct scientific measurements.

The project team is responsible for the final implementation, scientific interpretation, and submitted materials.

Conclusion

TerraTwin demonstrates how open scientific data and modern web technologies can help make space exploration research more accessible.

Our goal is to turn Earth into a practical laboratory for preparing the technologies of tomorrow's space missions.

TerraTwin — Discover Earth. Prepare for Space.
